claim: Partner rows are attached whatever rung printed the partner's name, so when a rule chip names a COMBINATION prescription by its order display (the ORDER rung), an answer naming just one constituent ('rifampin') now counts as naming the whole prescription, and the module no longer appends it as 'not named above'.
failure_mode: If merged as-is, a patient whose only rifampicin-bearing order is 'Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin' gets an answer saying 'it interacts with her rifampin [n]' returned with nothing appended and findingPartners {named:1, stated:1}. On base, containment fails and the module appends 'active order Isoniazid / pyrazinamide / rifampin'. This is a silent move toward non-reporting. ADR Decision 63 says a constituent does not name the prescription, and neither the README's nor ChartSearchService.FindingPartnerCoverage's residue list mentions it (they give only containment and the shared alias). Because statedPartners unions rows under the printed key, the isoniazid finding that prints the same prescription is also credited as stated by 'Rifampicin', though the answer never mentions isoniazid. Fix: attach rows only where the printed partner name is the ENTRY rung's reference label (the #555 gap), not an order display, which containment already handles. Or document this residue and pin it with a test.

claim: When StatedInteractionChips collapses two rule chips about one combination order (one per constituent), the surviving chip keeps only its own constituent's partner rows. So an answer naming one constituent is credited with naming the whole combination order, and an answer naming the other constituent is not. Which constituent counts depends on dataset order.
evidence: A throwaway test in the reference package, since deleted, used OneOrderNameAcrossOneResponseTest's fixture (ddi-combination-two-rules-one-note.json, order 'Emtricitabine / Tenofovir disoproxil', question 'Can I give her bedaquiline?') and drove the real validate(). It returned 1 chip, partners=[Emtricitabine / Tenofovir disoproxil], rowsOfPartner=[300195 Tenofovir disoproxil] only. namesThePartner('...her tenofovir disoproxil [1].')=true and namesThePartner('...her emtricitabine [1].')=false. isFirstStatementOf (StatedInteractionChips) drops the second chip before any row union. The PR unions rows only in collapseSharedMechanisms (DrugSafetyValidator.java:4779-4815). Recommended fix: attach partner rows only where the chip names the partner by an ENTRY label (the #555 shape), not on the ORDER rung where the printed name is her own prescription display. Containment already handles that display the way it did before this PR. Alternative: union the collapsed chip's rows into the survivor.

namesThePartner asks bare matchesText over the whole answer, so a partner alias that is only a word inside the SUBJECT drug's longer name, which every answer about that drug writes, counts as the answer naming her partner order. The completion and findingPartners then go silent for an order the prose never mentioned.
failure_mode: If merged as-is, on 'Can I give her magnesium salicylate?' with an active Salicylic acid order, an answer that names only magnesium salicylate no longer gets 'Also covered by those findings and not named above: active order Salicylic acid.' appended, and findingPartners reads {named:1, stated:1}. This happens because Salicylic acid's rows carry the alias 'salicylate', which matchesText finds inside 'magnesium salicylate'. Base appends the order and reports {1,0}. The same thing happens to the 'penicillin g' order on 'Can I give her procaine benzylpenicillin?' (alias 'benzylpenicillin'). This is a silent fail-open regression on the sentence that exists to name an interacting order the answer left out. It is not the residue the PR declares ('an alias the data files under two substances'): the answer never wrote a shared alias, it wrote the proposed drug's own name. Fix: ask #270's nested-name question, i.e. drop a partner occurrence (DrugReference.namedOccurrences) that sits inside an occurrence of another substance findImpliedByQuery reads in the answer (containedByAny, as substanceOwnsDose and isAboutTheEndedOrderDrug already do), and pin it with a magnesium-salicylate case.
evidence: Throwaway case in CitedFindingPartnerCompletionTest, using OverShippedData over the shipped KB through the real search(). At head: coverage {named=1, stated=1}, answer returned unchanged. Same chart and chips with validatorRaising(null, ...), which is containment only and so base semantics: {named=1, stated=0}, and 'Also covered by those findings and not named above: active order Salicylic acid.' is appended. Printed the partner rows DDInter1633/1634/2085: their aliases include 'salicylate' and 'magnesium salicylate tetrahydrate'. Procaine benzylpenicillin with orders Procaine + Benzylpenicillin: head {2,2}, containment {2,1} plus an appended 'active order penicillin g'. A separate KB sweep calling DrugReferenceService.findByQuery on each substance's own name found 79 of 2114 substances whose name also prose-matches another substance's row. That figure says how many names can trigger it, not how many rule pairs are affected. Precedent for the fix: DrugSafetyValidator.substanceOwnsDose (#270, containedByAny at line 13551) and isAboutTheEndedOrderDrug.
